weeks.rationale: Race week for HYROX on Sunday 02 Aug. Train lightly sharp Mon-Wed, then freshen over the final three days (Thu-Sat) — volume cut, one short race-pace opener, nothing heavy or exhausting — and race Sunday. This is a deliberate half-week freshen, not a full taper: the short Hyrox effort and the athlete's err-high bias justify keeping some sharpness in the legs.
weeks.methodology: The week applies the taper principle (cut volume, keep a touch of intensity) to arrive fresh without going flat, while protecting the easy days as genuinely easy. Sharpening is done with very short race-pace touches that prime neuromuscular readiness at low fatigue cost. No heavy barbell or explosive work inside the freshen window, since same-session and residual fatigue would blunt race-day power. Station touches stay at competition load but tiny volume for specificity without accumulation.

sessions.title: Easy Run + Strides
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy Z1; 25 min steady low Z2 (139-147 bpm, 5:15-5:20/km); 6x20s strides on feel with full walk-back; 5 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic maintenance with light neuromuscular sharpening.
sessions.why: Easy volume plus strides keeps the engine and turnover primed without fatigue; no more, because race week is about arriving fresh, not building fitness.

sessions.title: Race-Pace Primer
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy; 3 rounds of [400 m @ race pace ~4:55/km + one station light]: R1 ski erg 250 m, R2 sled push 12.5 m @ 202 kg, R3 wall balls x15 @ 9 kg; 8 min easy. Keep it crisp and well short of failure.
sessions.purpose: Rehearse race pace and transitions at very low volume.
sessions.why: A short compromised primer tunes race feel and pacing; kept tiny so it sharpens rather than fatigues three days out.

sessions.title: Light Full-Body Primer
sessions.prescription: Movement primer only, RPE 5-6, nothing heavy: goblet squat 3x8 @ light; band pull-apart 3x15; hip hinge 3x8 @ moderate; a few easy box step-ups. Grease the pattern, leave feeling fresher not tired.
sessions.purpose: Keep movement patterns sharp without adding fatigue.
sessions.why: A light primer maintains neuromuscular quality; heavy loading is deliberately dropped this week because residual strength fatigue would cost race-day power.

sessions.title: Shakeout + Strides
sessions.prescription: Freshen begins. 25 min very easy Z1 (<139 bpm) plus 4x15s relaxed strides. Should feel almost too easy.
sessions.purpose: Flush the legs and keep turnover without any load.
sessions.why: Very easy volume plus a few strides keeps blood flowing and legs snappy; anything harder now would eat into race-day freshness.

sessions.title: Rest / Mobility
sessions.prescription: Full rest or 15-20 min gentle mobility and a short walk. Hydrate, sleep, prep kit.
sessions.purpose: Deep recovery two days out.
sessions.why: A rest day inside the freshen window banks freshness for Sunday; there is no fitness to gain and real recovery to protect.

sessions.title: Pre-Race Opener
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy Z1-low Z2; 3x100 m @ race pace with full recovery; 5 min easy. Short, sharp, done well before fatigue.
sessions.purpose: Prime the system the day before the race.
sessions.why: A brief opener wakes up race pace and leaves the legs fresh; kept to a handful of short efforts so it activates without fatiguing.

sessions.title: HYROX — RACE DAY
sessions.prescription: Race. 8x1 km run alternated with the 8 stations at Men's Pro loads: ski erg 1000 m, sled push 50 m @ 202 kg, sled pull 50 m @ 153 kg, burpee broad jump 80 m, row 1000 m, farmers carry 200 m @ 2x32 kg, sandbag lunges 100 m @ 30 kg, wall balls x100 @ 9 kg to 3.0 m. Execute race plan; pace the opening runs, hold form through the sleds.
sessions.purpose: The A-race — execute the season's target.
sessions.why: Everything in the block points here; the job today is execution and pacing, not holding back.

weeks.rationale: The week after the race. Open Monday with a single easy recovery jog, then train through in-band for the rest of the week rather than taking a full recovery week (the athlete's stated preference). With ~15 weeks to the next Hyrox this returns to a base footing: aerobic volume with one controlled quality run and a return to heavy strength.
weeks.methodology: Base-phase emphasis on polarized, mostly-easy running volume rebuilds aerobic fitness after the race. One tempo session reintroduces quality without the sharpness of full threshold, and heavy lower-body strength returns for running economy — placed on its own day and separated from the hard run to keep hard days apart. Station work is folded into an easy day so Hyrox specificity continues at low interference.

sessions.title: Recovery Jog
sessions.prescription: Post-race flush: 30 min very easy Z1 (<139 bpm), conversational throughout. Walk if needed.
sessions.purpose: Active recovery the day after the race.
sessions.why: One easy day clears race fatigue while keeping the athlete moving; anything harder now would blunt recovery for the week ahead.

sessions.title: Easy Run + Strides
sessions.prescription: 12 min easy; 40 min steady low Z2 (139-147 bpm, 5:15-5:20/km); 6x20s strides; 5 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Rebuild aerobic volume on fresh legs.
sessions.why: Easy volume is the backbone of base phase; strides keep turnover without tipping into quality this early in the week.

sessions.title: Heavy Lower + Explosives
sessions.prescription: 10 min ramp. Back squat 4x3 @ 95 kg (ease back in, RPE 7-8); trap-bar deadlift 3x4 @ 130 kg RPE 8; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg; box jump 5x3 explosive full recovery; weighted step-up 3x8/leg @ 20 kg/hand.
sessions.purpose: Return heavy strength for running economy and sled power.
sessions.why: Heavy low-rep lifting drives economy with minimal added mass; loads are trimmed slightly the first week back to re-groove after race stress. Placed on its own day and off the hard run to avoid concurrent interference.

sessions.title: Tempo 3x8 min
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy build; 3x[8 min @ tempo (147-155 bpm, 5:04-4:48/km) + 2:30 jog easy]; 10 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Reintroduce quality below full threshold.
sessions.why: Tempo restores aerobic quality gently the first week back; kept short of full threshold so it stimulates without the cost of a hard LT2 session so soon after racing.

sessions.title: Easy Run + Upper Stations
sessions.prescription: 20 min easy Z2 run; then station/grip circuit sparing the legs: ski erg 4x250 m hard pull / 60s easy; pull-up 4x6 strict; farmers carry 200 m x3 @ 2x32 kg unbroken; wall balls 3x20 @ 9 kg.
sessions.purpose: Maintain Hyrox station fitness while sparing the legs.
sessions.why: Upper-body pull/grip station work keeps race specificity alive without loading the legs before the long run; easy running adds volume, not intensity.

sessions.title: Long Run
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy Z1; 80 min steady Z2 (139-147 bpm, 5:15-5:20/km); 5 min easy. Keep it out of the grey zone throughout.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic endurance for the 21k and Hyrox running.
sessions.why: The long run is the week's biggest aerobic stimulus; held strictly in Z2 so it builds endurance without the recovery cost of grey-zone running.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or a short walk.
sessions.purpose: Complete recovery.
sessions.why: A planned rest day protects adaptation and keeps the easy days easy; nothing is gained by filling it.

weeks.rationale: A full base week with the next Hyrox 14 weeks out. Aerobic volume dominates, with one true threshold session to start raising LT2 again and one heavy strength day, spaced so the two hard days are separated by an easy run. Saturday's long run carries a short race-pace finish to rehearse pace on tired legs.
weeks.methodology: Polarized structure: two hard poles (Tuesday threshold to raise LT2, Thursday heavy/explosive strength for economy) with every other run genuinely easy and the grey zone avoided. Hard days are separated by an easy aerobic day to respect recovery. Station work sits on an easy day, and explosive lifting is kept off the hard-run day to avoid same-session interference. The long run stays aerobic except a controlled race-pace finish.

sessions.title: Easy Run + Strides
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy; 40 min steady low Z2 (139-147 bpm, 5:15-5:20/km); 6x20s strides; 5 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic base with light turnover.
sessions.why: Easy volume builds the aerobic engine; strides keep leg speed without adding a hard day.

sessions.title: Threshold 4x8 min
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy build; 4x[8 min @ threshold (155-163 bpm, 4:48-4:34/km) + 2:30 jog]; 10 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Raise LT2 — the shared lever for 21k and Hyrox running.
sessions.why: A full threshold dose lifts the aerobic ceiling; it is the week's one hard run, keeping the intensity distribution polarized.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy Z1; 35 min steady low Z2 (139-143 bpm); 5 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Active recovery between the two hard days.
sessions.why: An easy day separates Tuesday's threshold from Thursday's heavy lift so both hard sessions are done fresh; kept cleanly easy, not grey.

sessions.title: Heavy Lower + Explosives
sessions.prescription: 10 min ramp. Back squat 5x3 @ 100 kg RPE 8; trap-bar deadlift 4x4 @ 130 kg RPE 8; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg; box jump 5x3 explosive; weighted step-up 3x8/leg @ 20 kg/hand.
sessions.purpose: Maximal strength and power for running economy and sled push.
sessions.why: Heavy, low-rep lifting improves economy with little added mass; progress the load when a top set leaves >2 RIR. Kept off the hard-run day so explosive quality isn't blunted by concurrent fatigue.

sessions.title: Easy Run + Stations
sessions.prescription: 25 min easy Z2 run; then stations at race load: sled push 4x12.5 m @ 202 kg; sandbag lunges 100 m @ 30 kg; wall balls 3x20 @ 9 kg to 3.0 m.
sessions.purpose: Hyrox lower-body station specificity on fresh-ish legs.
sessions.why: Sled and lunge work at competition load keeps Hyrox specificity; paired with easy running so it adds race-specific load without a second hard running stimulus.

sessions.title: Long Run + Race-Pace Finish
sessions.prescription: 15 min easy Z1; 60 min steady Z2 (139-147 bpm); 3x[5 min @ race pace ~4:55/km upper Z3 + 3 min jog]; 5 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Endurance plus race pace on fatigued legs.
sessions.why: The long run drives aerobic endurance; a short race-pace finish rehearses goal pace under fatigue without turning the whole run into a hard session.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or a short walk.
sessions.purpose: Complete recovery.
sessions.why: A planned rest day protects adaptation and keeps the easy days easy; nothing is gained by filling it.

weeks.rationale: Second full base week, 13 weeks out. Volume holds near base with an equal split between pure running quality and Hyrox specificity: a compromised-running interval session mid-week and a long run at the weekend, plus the heavy strength day. Hard days remain separated by easy running.
weeks.methodology: Continues polarized base training: easy volume dominant, with a compromised-running session that trains running under station fatigue (Hyrox-specific) and a heavy strength day for economy. The two hard days are separated by an easy aerobic run, explosive lifting stays off the hard-run day, and the long run holds Z2. Station loads remain at competition standard for specificity.

sessions.title: Easy Run + Strides
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy; 40 min steady low Z2 (139-147 bpm, 5:15-5:20/km); 6x20s strides; 5 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic base with light turnover.
sessions.why: Easy volume maintains the engine; strides keep leg speed without a hard day.

sessions.title: Compromised Running 4x1 km
sessions.prescription: 12 min easy. 4 rounds of [1000 m @ threshold-to-race pace (150-160 bpm, ~4:55/km) + one station at race load]: R1 sled push 25 m @ 202 kg, R2 farmers carry 200 m @ 2x32 kg, R3 wall balls x30 @ 9 kg, R4 sandbag lunges 50 m @ 30 kg. 8 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Rehearse running under station-induced fatigue.
sessions.why: Compromised running is the most Hyrox-specific run stimulus and doubles as quality; it is the week's hard run, so the rest of the week's running stays easy.

sessions.title: Easy Aerobic
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy Z1; 40 min steady low Z2 (139-143 bpm); 5 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Active recovery and volume between hard days.
sessions.why: An easy day separates Tuesday's compromised session from Thursday's heavy lift; kept cleanly easy to protect both hard days.

sessions.title: Heavy Lower + Explosives
sessions.prescription: 10 min ramp. Back squat 5x3 @ 100 kg RPE 8; trap-bar deadlift 4x4 @ 132 kg RPE 8; hip thrust 3x8 @ 110 kg; hurdle hop 5x3 explosive; weighted step-up 3x8/leg @ 20 kg/hand.
sessions.purpose: Maintain maximal strength and power for economy.
sessions.why: Heavy lifting sustains economy gains; deadlift nudges up since last week's top sets left reserve. Kept off the hard-run day to protect explosive quality.

sessions.title: Easy Run
sessions.prescription: 10 min easy; 30 min steady low Z2 (139-147 bpm); 5 min easy. Optional 4 strides.
sessions.purpose: Easy volume before the long run.
sessions.why: A cleanly easy day adds aerobic volume and keeps the legs fresh for Saturday's long run.

sessions.prescription: 15 min easy Z1; 80 min steady Z2 (139-147 bpm, 5:15-5:20/km); 5 min easy.
sessions.purpose: Aerobic endurance for 21k and Hyrox running.
sessions.why: The long run is the week's largest aerobic dose; held in Z2 to build endurance without grey-zone recovery cost.

sessions.title: Rest
sessions.prescription: Full rest. Optional light mobility or a short walk.
